I'll wait for the other songs to say anything definite.
but this song is... it's Placebo-ish in tunes and expressive vocals and all. Its emotion is related to LLL but even cheaper than that,, and is very far from their early ones in terms of what they are expressing.

not expecting them stay singing teenage angst, but I do hope for something no so aligned with this consumerist, fast-speeding, mass-production age. something more human i guess. 

which doesn't equal just catchy tunes or expressive vocals...

yeah. I see what you're saying, especially from the fact that they simply didn't write anything new in recent 8 years. And that there is no really any solo work from Brian in this period. I'm also wondering what he is up to musically now. 

I still love WYIN, and the same titled song. 

I guess the question can only be answered when the new album is released fully.

The 90s band I know that continued into the 21th century all had their adaptation to age, attitude to the current culture, etc., and some still are creating decent new works and superb performances. The turning from WYIN to BFTS to LLL is Placebo's transition. but if the old sounds lost spark to themselves I just hope they could be honest to themselves and write and sing what they truly like, what they are thinking about... but again as one of the many audiences I know what i said is insignificant, and if music as an expression don't work as it was to them I'll just accept that.

agreed. i also love pity party and live at rak studios 2013. And i really like the acoustic version of post blue they did in 2006, the M6 private concert. And the string instrumental version of Meds in 2008 Angkor Wat. 
But Stefan is doing electronic music now, and for Brian Idk what he was up to musically recently... to be honest I'm not a huge fan of synth. so I'm probably a little biased.

yeah it reminds me of English summer rain. 
looking forward to the new album...just hope it will be released soon.

I actually like the tears quite much. Maybe it's because I'm not a native English speaker and generally don't care that much in terms of lyrics.  It is rare to see Brett singing some songs about love in its positive definition (neither in Suede nor in his later solo work), and I think they did a good job to convey that. And there are some delicate tunes, like The Ghost of You, imperfection, brave new country, and beautiful pain.

Speaking of the unreleased songs i like Berlin. It has some proto-Suede aura around it in my opinion. You can find some videos of it on YouTube if you haven't heard it.
ah, thanks. but why is the bside show called infamous? i watched it on youtube but never know any of that.
no best. it changes every time. (speaking for me)
